steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).

Beat butter, white sugar, and brown sugar together with an electric mixer in a large bowl until light and fluffy. Beat first egg into butter mixture. Beat second egg into mixture along with vanilla extract.

Combine flour, baking soda, and salt together in a separate bowl; stir into butter mixture until just combined. Fold in chocolate chips and coconut. Drop spoonfuls of dough 2 inches apart onto ungreased cookie sheets.
Bake in the preheated oven until edges are golden, about 8 to 10 minutes. Cool on the cookie sheets briefly before removing to a wire rack to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: Chococonut Chip Cookies
raw_recipe.description: This coconut-chocolate chip cookie recipe makes dozens of delicious drop cookies using pantry staples, semisweet chocolate chips, and flaked coconut.

review.reviewBody: These cookies are freaking awesome. Adding an additional 1/2 stick of butter and 2 tablespoons of milk makes them super fluffy and chewwwy. They come out rather flat otherwise.
With this recipe my cookies kept coming out flat so I took another reviewer's advice and added 1/2 stick of butter and it helped a lot. I'm sharing and eating these cookies!

Y'all should be honored this is my first time leaving a review bc I DO love it- but here's the tweaks first! * Add 1tbs corn starch to make fluffy ITS MY SECRET WEAPON * Put dough in freezer before baking for fluff * Used 1 3/4 sugar bc SWEETENED coconut is sooo sweet my dudes MY ADDITIONS/TWEAKS: I used 1/2c butter and 1/2c (unrefined) coconut oil. Why? I love me some coconut and butter is expensive and I lack the dough (pun intended) I use it for salt scrubs mostly. It's a rock, melted in microwave first but it got a little too warm- so butter was straight from fridge. Parchment paper on pan bc why not. Used dark chocolate chips to balance out sweet. (Using electric oven) Took 12 mins to cook to perfection~ After everything, they did spread but that's to be expected -from coconut oil- so if you use straight butter with cornstarch it'll be fine! Made 1.5-2tbs balls and they spread to about 3". ***Anyways, 4stars bc I like them fluffy and not spread thin so cornstarch is a must. Overall it was a success!!

I read all the previous reviews and tweaked the original just a bit ! Do these changes ! They really are the best cookie I've had in along time and I will make another batch of these fantastic taste treats before Christmas ! 

11/2 cups of softened butter
3 cups of coconut 
1tablespoon of coconut extract 
1cup of chopped pecans 
1cup of semisweet chocolate chips and
1cup of butterscotch chips 
Bake at 350 for 10 min or till edges are brown 
YUMMY!!

This recipe is an instant favourite for us. These are AMAZING!! I subbed out half of the white sugar with coconut sugar, and changed the brown sugar to golden sugar to balance out the flavour as coconut sugar is already deep and rich. Thank you for this recipe!

I only had half the chocolate suggested so I added 1/2 tsp cardamom powder and 1/2 tsp cinnamon powder and they came out great. I cooked exactly 8 min and thought they looked under cooked but I wanted to make sure they stayed soft. They were perfect after cooling completely if u love a chewy cookie. I will definitely be making them again and didn't even miss the other cup of chocolate chips I left out. Thx

I made 21 larger cookies that took about twenty minutes to bake on convection setting. I chilled the dough for a few hours before baking to allow the flavors to blend and perhaps reduce spreading and I think it worked because they came out with a nice dome shape. Used unsweetened coconut. A crowd pleaser!

Loving how CRISP these turn out. They are a little sticky to work with but believe me, it’s worth the trouble. I toasted the coconut and added a cup of walnuts. Next time I make these my plan is to substitute 1/2 cup of oats for 1/2 cup of the flour.

I should add that I used butter flavored crisco instead of butter, which got around the 'flat' issue that some mentioned in the recipe. Instead of using chocolate chips I added chopped pecans instead --- WoNDERFUL!! One of the best coconut pecan cookies I've had. Will definitely make these again :)

I used one less cup of flour substituting with 1 cup of oats. Also added 1/2 - 2/3 cup of dried cranberries and half milk chocolate and half semi sweet chocolate chips. Got very good reviews from family who liked it.

I did make three changes.
 1) butter flavor crisco instead of butter (Fluffier texture)
2) almond extract instead of vanilla 
3) 1/2 t additional salt to offset sweetness of coconut.
Mmm...Think almond joy:-)

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Takes Chocolate Chip Cookies to a Whole New Level! These cookies take chocolate chips to a whole new level! The chocolate and coconut combination is delicious, and the recipe is easy to follow. I baked mine for 10–11 minutes, and they came out perfectly—soft, chewy, and delicious. Next time, I may replace the vanilla extract with coconut extract to give them even more coconut flavor, but they're great flavors just as the recipe is written. This one is definitely a keeper! It's a family favorite and a real crowd-pleaser. Worth the effort and I'll absolutely make them again! 🥥🍫🍪
***** BOMB***** This is a great recipe! I added a tsp of corn starch from another comment here.
I thought I had the best choc chip cookie recipe. ...Now I do !! It's the right amt of coconut. Really delicious !! Highly recommend you to try!!!
Added the extra butter and a pinch of cornstarch and they were AMAZING! Fluffy and chewy. I only cooked them 8 mins and they were perfect!
Loved the combination of coconut and dark choc chips. I used shredded coconut as I didn't have flaked coconut. Definitely will make it again. 💞
Wow these are great. Flavorful and unique yet familiar. Thanks for creating this recipe, I am really loving it. The coconut brings a nice sweet taste that isnt overly sugary.
Really simple, can't mess it up. Always comes out delicious, even my friends who don't like coconut enjoy

I added the 1/3 cup coconut oil, very tasty. I also added a little extra flour just incase they would spread too much, that was not necessary, proofed up a little. Cut back the salt to 3/4 teaspoon. Next time I might add more vanilla - or just enjoy them with ice cream. Great addition to the traditional chocolate chip cookie.
